# hinge

A desktop scrcpy client that mirrors a Galaxy Z Fold 7 onto a placeholder phone model

## Development setup

No published releases yet. From a checkout of this repository:

```sh
npm install
npm run fetch-vendor
```

`fetch-vendor` downloads and checksums the bundled `adb` (Android platform-tools
r37.0.1) and `scrcpy-server-v4.1` into `vendor/` (gitignored). Pass `--only win` or
`--only linux` to fetch one platform.

## Status

Early development, M1 (flat mirror). The app connects to a phone over adb, starts scrcpy-server 4.1, and shows the video feed on a placeholder phone slab with touch and keyboard input routed back to the device. Folding reactions, the 3D showcase view, and packaged releases are later milestones.

## Running

```sh
npm run dev
```

connects to whatever device `adb` sees. Relevant flags:

- `--serial <id>` pick a device when more than one is attached
- `--replay <file.hrec>` play back a recorded session instead of a live device
- `--record <file.hrec>` mirror a live device and also write the session (video
  and posture samples) to a recording file
- `--probe` run a one-off hardware survey: waits for a device, collects `adb`
  property and `dumpsys` output, checks the scrcpy display list, and samples
  `device_state`/rotation while you fold and rotate the phone. Writes a JSON
  report to the desktop, or to the path given with `--out <file>`
- `--seconds <n>` how long `--probe` samples for (default 90)

A bare file name given to `--record` or `--out` (no directory in the path)
lands on the desktop; a path with a directory is used as given.

Each run writes `hinge.log` to the app's logs directory (truncated at
startup, no rotation) with server output, connection attempts and errors.
An error shown in the window or the probe result page names the log file.

### Windows

From a `cmd.exe` prompt in the installed or unpacked directory:

```bat
hinge.exe --serial 10.0.0.23:5555
hinge.exe --probe --seconds 60
```

The window is frameless; close it with Alt+F4 or from the taskbar.

## Development commands

```sh
npm run dev          # electron-vite dev server
npm run build         # production build
npm run typecheck     # tsc -b
npm test              # vitest
npm run test:e2e       # playwright, replays a synthetic recording end to end
npm run pack:win       # unpacked Windows build in dist/win-unpacked
npm run pack:linux     # unpacked Linux build in dist/linux-unpacked
```
